slides.say: For every number t, diamond of t is equal to t squared. In the choices, x is zero or more. Which of the following is not always true?

The diamond is in every choice, two or three times. That's a lot of work. So a tip first. In the exam, skip it, solve the rest of the section, and come back at the end. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, with algebra, and then plugging in numbers.
[short pause] Let's start with algebra. The diamond squares its input. Choice number one, six x squared is thirty-six x squared, and thirty-six times x squared is the same. True. Out.
Choice number two, root x squared is x, and x times x is x squared. True. Out. Choice number four, x minus seven and seven minus x are opposites, and squared they're equal. True. Out.
Choice number three, five x squared is twenty-five x squared, but five times x squared is only five x squared. Not equal. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way, and it's faster. What's different? No opening at all, just numbers. x is one. Choice number one, diamond of six is thirty-six, and thirty-six times diamond of one is thirty-six. Choice number two, one equals one. Choice number four, negative six and six squared are both thirty-six.

Choice number three, diamond of five is twenty-five, and five times diamond of one is five. Not equal, choice number three. One warning. Zero or one can make a false rule look true. If two choices had survived, we'd try a second number, like two. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
